subject: AI & Agents
title: Self-Driving Cars: How Close Are We?
description: A quick, practical guide to Self-Driving Cars: How Close Are We?.

hook.text: A car with no driver weaves through downtown San Francisco traffic. It's a regular Tuesday.

buildup.text: Autonomous vehicles use cameras, LIDAR, radar, and AI to perceive and navigate roads.

discovery.text: The AI must handle millions of edge cases — jaywalkers, construction zones, erratic drivers.

twist.text: Level 5 (fully autonomous anywhere) remains elusive. Most systems still need safety drivers.

climax.text: Waymo operates driverless taxis in multiple cities, but only in mapped, geofenced areas.

punchline.text: Self-driving works — in the places it's been taught.

quiz.question: Why can't current self-driving cars operate everywhere?
options: They need pre-mapped areas and struggle with edge cases
Laws prohibit them in all locations

details.summary: Self-driving cars use AI to perceive their surroundings through cameras, LIDAR, and radar, then make driving decisions in real time. Full autonomy is advancing but remains limited to specific areas and conditions.
details.whyItMatters: Autonomous vehicles promise to reduce accidents, traffic, and emissions. Understanding the current state of self-driving technology separates genuine progress from marketing hype.
takeaways: Self-driving cars combine cameras, LIDAR, and radar with AI
Full autonomy works in limited areas and ideal conditions
Waymo and Cruise operate commercial robotaxi services in some cities

faq.question: How close are we to fully self-driving cars?
faq.answer: Limited self-driving taxis operate in cities like Phoenix and San Francisco. Fully autonomous driving in all conditions everywhere remains years to decades away, depending on who you ask.

faq.question: Are self-driving cars safer than human drivers?
faq.answer: In their operating domains, companies report fewer accidents per mile than human drivers. But direct comparison is difficult since autonomous cars avoid the challenging conditions where most crashes occur.
